script.title: How a Slow Harbour Collision Triggered a Historic Blast
script.hook_text: The Largest Blast Before Atomic Power
sentences: A slow harbour collision triggered the largest human-made explosion of its time.
In December 1917, the freighter Mont-Blanc collided with another ship in Halifax Harbour.
Mont-Blanc was fully loaded with high explosives and fuel.
Sparks ignited spilled fuel on deck, engulfing the vessel in flames.
Unaware of the danger, curious citizens gathered at nearby windows to watch.
Twenty minutes later, the ship detonated with the energy of 2.9 kilotons of TNT.
It obliterated everything within a half-mile radius in seconds.
script.description: The story of the 1917 Halifax Explosion, the largest human-made blast of its time.
claims_en: In December 1917, the SS Mont-Blanc collided with the SS Imo in Halifax Harbour.
Mont-Blanc was fully loaded with high explosives and fuel.
Sparks from the collision ignited spilled benzol fuel on deck.
Spectators gathered at windows and streets to watch the ship fire.
Around twenty minutes after the collision, Mont-Blanc exploded releasing energy equivalent to roughly 2.9 kilotons of TNT.
The explosion was the largest human-made blast at the time.
Nearly all structures within a half-mile radius were obliterated.
